original_question: For any two superpartitions Lambda and Omega of the same degree, does the normalized Macdonald superpolynomial satisfy the symmetry identity P_tilde_Lambda(u_Omega) = P_tilde_Omega(u_Lambda), where u_Lambda denotes the specialization determined by Lambda?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the specialization/symmetry conjecture for Macdonald superpolynomials in superspace: the superspace analogue of the ordinary Macdonald symmetry u_λ(P̃_μ)=u_μ(P̃_λ). In the review arXiv:1903.07777 this appears as part of the Macdonald-polynomial open-problem discussion, but the nearest fully explicit official formulation I could verify is Appendix B, Conjecture 2 (“Symmetry property”), together with the immediately preceding definition of the specialization u_Λ and the normalization by u_∅(P_Λ).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right phenomenon: a symmetry identity for Macdonald superpolynomials in superspace, indexed by two superpartitions Λ and Ω, involving a normalization of P_Λ and an evaluation/specialization map u_Λ attached to a superpartition.
missing_details: The superpartitions must have the same full superspace degree (n|m), not merely the same ordinary total degree n; in particular they must have the same fermionic degree m.

The ambient setting should be stated: symmetric superpolynomials in commuting variables x=(x1,x2,...) and anticommuting variables θ=(θ1,θ2,...) over the coefficient field Q(q,t), with θiθj = -θjθi and θi^2 = 0.
The Macdonald superpolynomials P_Λ(x,θ;q,t) should be identified as the triangular-and-orthogonal basis in superspace, so the object under discussion is unambiguous.
The normalization must be given explicitly: P̃_Λ := P_Λ / u_∅(P_Λ), where ∅ = (δ_m; ) and δ_m = (m-1,m-2,...,1,0).
The specialization u_Λ must be defined explicitly, not only named: u_Λ(F) = [ (∂_{θ1}⋯∂_{θm} F(x;θ)) / Δ_m(x) ]_{x_i = v_i}, with Δ_m(x) = ∏_{1≤i<j≤m} (x_i - x_j).
The specialization points v_i should be specified: v_{σ^{-1}(i)} = q^{-Λ_i^*} t^{i-1}, where σ is a permutation rearranging Λ into Λ^*.
The quantifier should say explicitly that the identity is asked for every pair Λ, Ω of superpartitions of the same degree (n|m), for all admissible parameters q and t in the paper’s generic setting.
refined_question: Let P_Λ(x,θ;q,t) be the Macdonald superpolynomial in superspace over Q(q,t), indexed by a superpartition Λ of degree (n|m), and let u_Λ be the specialization defined on symmetric superpolynomials of fermionic degree m by u_Λ(F) = [ (∂_{θ1}⋯∂_{θm}F(x;θ)) / Δ_m(x) ]_{x_i=v_i}, where Δ_m(x)=∏_{1≤i<j≤m}(x_i-x_j) and the specialization points satisfy v_{σ^{-1}(i)} = q^{-Λ_i^*} t^{i-1} for a permutation σ sending Λ to Λ^*. If ∅=(δ_m; ) with δ_m=(m-1,m-2,...,1,0) and P̃_Λ := P_Λ / u_∅(P_Λ), is it true that for every pair of superpartitions Λ and Ω of the same degree (n|m), one has u_Λ(P̃_Ω) = u_Ω(P̃_Λ)?
justification: The core of your draft is right: it is aiming at the superspace analogue of the ordinary Macdonald symmetry property. The nearest precise formulation I could verify defines u_Λ and the normalization immediately before stating the symmetry conjecture. I kept the normalized version because that is the paper-faithful way to make the conjecture stand alone: the nearby context introduces normalization by u_∅(P_Λ), and the ordinary Macdonald analogue quoted earlier in the same source is stated for normalized polynomials. I did not broaden the question beyond this exact specialization/symmetry problem, and I did not add variants not explicitly supplied by the surrounding source material.
